subject: Revenue protection vs discount tradeoff — VP/CFO approval requested
messages:
From: Elaine Moore <elaine.moore@veridianhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot pricing — procurement constraints

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up with procurement this morning and they pushed back on the pricing for the proposed pilot footprint. To get to an approved PO they asked if Redwood can offer: a 25% first-year commercial discount or a $120k onboarding credit applied to year one.

Our timeline is tight — procurement needs terms and an indicative commercial memo by EOD Friday (10/02). This is a strategic pilot for us; if we can land agreeable economics they are prepared to commit to a 24-month expansion path.

Can your team accelerate a commercial exception review? If helpful, I can loop our CFO on signoff.

—Elaine
Elaine Moore
Head of Partnerships, Veridian Health
elaine.moore@veridianhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Moore <elaine.moore@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot pricing — procurement constraints

Elaine — thanks for the context and the clear timelines.

Short answer: we can get you commercial terms for review by EOD Friday, but a 25% recurring first-year discount would materially damage unit economics unless paired with a firm 24-month commitment and an onboarding cap.

Proposed immediate options (indicative):
- Option A (preferred): 18% recurring discount year 1 + $75k one-time onboarding credit; 24-month committed term, minimum annual spend $450k.
- Option B (if procurement insists on $120k credit): $120k onboarding credit but discount limited to 12% year 1; 24-month committed term and no additional onboarding credits thereafter.

I need to escalate both options for VP/CFO signoff — copying our Commercial and Finance leads internally. Putting a short commercial memo and price impact calc in a follow-up.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: veridian_sow_draft.pdf (stub), price_impact_calc.xlsx (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Veridian — request for commercial exception (need VP/CFO signoff)

Team — forwarding a procurement ask from Veridian (attached). They are requesting a 25% first-year discount OR a $120k onboarding credit to sign a 24-month pilot + expansion path. Key commercials:
- Target ARR (year 1 run-rate): ~$650k; committed minimum yearly spend requested: $450k.
- Deployment: dedicated private cluster (Redwood Private) with higher infra cost profile.
- Strategic signal: Veridian is well connected in the Northeast provider space — high expansion probability if pilot works.

Why I’m escalating:
- 25% recurring discount would reduce gross margins below our acceptable threshold for Private deployments given expected infra profile (see attached calc).
- $120k one-time credit is less margin-disruptive but still large; we can consider a capped onboarding credit that phases with milestones.

Asks:
1) Marcus — can Commercial approve Option A (18% + $75k credit + 24mo commitment) as our negotiation anchor?
2) Karthik — do you see any risk with making the contract 24-month committed with monthly true-ups?
3) Markus — need VP/CFO sign-off on any concession beyond $75k onboarding (or >18% discount).

I’ve attached: veridian_sow_draft.pdf and price_impact_calc.xlsx (sensitivity calc on discount vs EBITDA impact). Procurement wants an updated memo to share with their procurement committee by EOD 10/02 — tight but doable if we get rapid alignment.

Thanks —
Marissa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Veridian — request for commercial exception (need VP/CFO signoff)

Marissa — I reviewed the calc. Short notes:
- Veridian's expansion profile is attractive; I support a measured concession to land the pilot.
- Option A (18% + $75k) is where Commercial is comfortable subject to Finance approval. We should lock the 24-month term with minimum committed ARR and include a quarterly usage review to rebaseline.
- We should tie the onboarding credit to milestones: 50% on SOW signature, 50% on pilot completion/metrics (uptime and 3 production use-cases).

Markus — our ask is to authorize up to $75k onboarding credit + 18% first-year discount for RDW-2026-1397, conditional on 24-month committed term and exclusion of other credits. If Finance can stretch to $120k credit only with stricter guardrails (e.g., higher commit or accelerated payments), please advise.

I'll draft the commercial memo for Elaine once we have signoff.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Veridian — request for commercial exception (need VP/CFO signoff)

Team — after reviewing the sensitivity model: approved with constraints.

Finance position (approved):
- Approve Option A: 18% recurring first-year discount + $75k one-time onboarding credit.
- Condition: 24-month minimum committed term with a $450k annual minimum; prepayment of the first 6 months OR an accelerated payment schedule (Net 30 on first invoice).
- Onboarding credit to be milestone-driven (as Marcus suggested). No other stacking credits allowed.
- Legal to add a clause that allows us to reclaim a pro rata portion of the credit if they terminate before 12 months.

If Procurement insists on $120k credit, Finance will only consider it if Veridian provides a minimum 36-month committed ARR or an increased annual minimum (>$650k), which is unlikely on this pilot.

Marissa — please proceed to send the updated memo to Elaine with Option A as the company position and include the conditions above. Ensure Legal & Contracts get looped on SOW language around reclaimability.

Markus Klein
VP Finance, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Moore <elaine.moore@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot pricing — commercial memo attached

Elaine — thank you for your patience. Attached is our commercial position per internal approvals. Key points:
- Option A (company-preferred): 18% recurring discount year 1 + $75k onboarding credit; 24-month committed term; $450k annual minimum; onboarding credit paid in two milestone tranches.
- Conditions: first six months prepayment or Net 30 accelerated first invoice; milestone language to be reflected in SOW; credit reclaimable pro rata if they terminate before 12 months.

If procurement cannot accept Option A, let me know and I will request Finance to consider the $120k credit scenario, but that will require a materially larger commitment (36 months or >$650k annual minimum).

Next steps:
1) If Option A is acceptable, confirm and I’ll send a redlined SOW with the milestone schedule and payment terms for your procurement committee.
2) If procurement needs the $120k credit path, share their must-haves so I can re-escalate.

Best —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
